critical_code_review_comments: bookings.py:330 — RCA: motor's `insert_one(base_doc)` mutates `base_doc` in place, assigning a new `ObjectId` to `base_doc['_id']`. The recurrence loop then spread `**base_doc` into every occurrence, meaning EVERY sibling ended up with the SAME `_id`, so the second sibling insert raised DuplicateKeyError. Fixed by explicitly popping `_id` before the loop; alternative would be to build sibling dicts from the pydantic payload rather than from `base_doc`.
bookings.py:389 — `update_series` correctly EXCLUDES start_at/end_at from the propagation because siblings sit on different timestamps; verified by test_series_update_propagates_metadata_not_times.
bookings.py:423 — `delete_series` matches by `id == parent_id OR parent_booking_id == parent_id`, so both the root and every sibling are wiped in one call. Verified.

bookings.py:517 — delete_room refuses when *any* show references the studio (not just future ones). This is a safe default but may surprise users if legacy/past shows still reference the studio; consider filtering by `date >= today` if that becomes noisy.

bookings.py:57-121 — find_room_conflict correctly treats bookings and shows as peers: only `blocks_room=True` on BOTH sides triggers a conflict; half-open intervals let back-to-back slots coexist. Legacy shows without the field default to blocking via `$ne: False`, which is the right migration story.

RoomBookingsPage.js:31 — Missing hook (see frontend_issues) was a compile blocker; unfixed it would have hidden EVERY functional bug behind the CRA error overlay. This is exactly the kind of import that must be caught by lint/CI before merge.

rca of the issue: Root cause of the 500 during recurring booking creation: Motor's `insert_one(base_doc)` mutates the dict in place, adding a `_id: ObjectId(...)` field. The subsequent recurrence loop built each sibling via `{**base_doc, 'id': str(uuid4()), ...}` — but that spread also copied the mutated `_id`. On the very first sibling insert, MongoDB rejected the duplicate `_id` with E11000. Reproduction: POST /api/bookings with recurrence_type='weekly' + a recurrence_end_date >7 days out → 500 (verifiable in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log — 'pymongo.errors.DuplicateKeyError'). Mitigation applied: `base_doc.pop('_id', None)` immediately after the parent insert, before the sibling loop; each sibling now gets a fresh `_id` from mongo. Alternative long-term fix: build a fresh dict per occurrence (dict comprehension over the pydantic payload) rather than spreading a document that has round-tripped through Motor. Verified by rerunning the entire suite → 19/19 pass.
